name: lilbee-mcp-wiki
description: Builds, reads and lints the generated lilbee wiki (concept, entity and synthesis pages with citations). Use only when the user asks about wiki, concept, entity or synthesis pages, or when lilbee status shows a built wiki. Needs the lilbee-mcp skill for how to reach lilbee.
---

# lilbee wiki

The wiki layer writes per-concept and per-entity pages, with citations, from the indexed
library. It is opt-in and rough. Skip it unless the user asks about wiki pages or the
library status already shows a built wiki. The `lilbee-mcp` skill says how to reach lilbee
(MCP tools or `lilbee --json`) and how to cite.

## Availability

`lilbee_wiki_status` (CLI `lilbee --json wiki status`) always works. It reports
`wiki_enabled` and the page counts. `lilbee_wiki_wipe` is always present too, because
turning the wiki off leaves the generated pages in place. Every other wiki tool is absent
from the MCP tool list when the server started with the wiki off, and returns
`{"error": "wiki not enabled"}` if the wiki is turned off while it runs. Enabling the wiki
with a settings change takes effect after the user restarts the MCP server. The CLI
commands do not need a restart.

With the wiki off, the CLI commands that write (`build`, `update`, `synthesize`, `prune`,
`index`, `generate`, `drafts accept`, `drafts reject`) exit with "Wiki is disabled (set
wiki = true in settings)". The CLI has no settings command: ask the user to set
`wiki = true` in `config.toml` or on the `/settings` screen of `lilbee chat`.

## Commands

Each MCP tool has a CLI twin: `lilbee_wiki_<name>` is `lilbee --json wiki <name>`.

| Task | Name | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Build the whole wiki | `build` (`--dry-run` previews candidates) | Long, one LLM call per source |
| Refresh after a sync | `update` | Long, currently a full rebuild |
| Cross-source pages | `synthesize` (concept clusters with three or more sources) | Long |
| Rebuild the browse index | `index` | Short, no LLM call |
| Write one indexed page | `generate <slug>` | One LLM call |
| Archive stale pages | `prune` | Short |
| Delete every generated page | `wipe` (MCP `confirm=true`, CLI `--yes`) | Short, cannot be undone |
| Inspect | `status`, `list`, `read <slug>`, `lint`, `citations`, `drafts list`, `drafts diff <slug>` | Short |

A dry run of `build` makes no LLM call, so it is short.

## Flow

1. Read the wiki status. If a wiki exists, skip the build.
2. Run `build` as a long operation: use a subagent or background mechanism if the host has
   one, otherwise run it in the foreground and wait. Do not search meanwhile. See the
   long-operation rule in the `lilbee-mcp` skill.
3. List the pages, then check the drafts list for pages that await review.
4. Search the wiki with `lilbee_search(..., scope="wiki")` or
   `lilbee --json search "query" --scope wiki`. Cite wiki pages as the search reports them.
5. Run `lint` to find orphan pages and stale citations.

Accepting or rejecting a draft changes the wiki the user sees. Do it only when the user
asks. The MCP tools only list and diff drafts. Accept and reject are CLI only:
`lilbee --json wiki drafts accept <slug>` and `lilbee --json wiki drafts reject <slug>`.
Run `wipe` only when the user asks.

name: lilbee-mcp
description: Searches the user's local lilbee knowledge base (indexed code, documents, PDFs and crawled pages) and answers with file and line citations. Use when the user asks about their own files, code or docs, or asks to index, crawl or remove content. Works through lilbee MCP tools when connected, or the lilbee command line with --json when not.

# lilbee

[lilbee](https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee) is a local retrieval engine. It indexes the
user's files into a `.lilbee/` store. The data stays on the user's machine. Only the text
you quote leaves it. By default, search may ask the chat model for query variants (it skips
very short queries), so it can be slow while that model is busy.

## When to use it

Reach for lilbee first when the user asks where something is, how something in their own
code or documents works, or what a document says. Web-fetch and file-read tools cannot see
the index. Do not use lilbee as a web search or as a code editor.

## How to reach it

Pick one path and stay on it.

- **MCP.** If your tool list has tools from the lilbee MCP server, call them. The host adds
  its own prefix to the tool name, so look for a tool whose name contains `lilbee` and ends
  in the tool name, such as `search` (for example `lilbee_search`, `mcp__lilbee__search` or
  `mcp__plugin_lilbee_lilbee__search`). The table below uses the `lilbee_` form.
- **CLI.** Otherwise run `lilbee --json <command>` in a shell. Each command prints one JSON
  object per line. An error exits non-zero with `{"error": "..."}`. If `lilbee` is not on
  the PATH, tell the user to install it. Do not guess another path.

| Step | MCP | CLI |
|---|---|---|
| Check the library | `lilbee_status` | `lilbee --json status` |
| Search | `lilbee_search` | `lilbee --json search "query" --top-k 12` |
| Add content | `lilbee_add` | `lilbee --json add <path or URL>...` |
| Re-index after edits | `lilbee_sync` | `lilbee --json sync` |
| Remove content | `lilbee_remove` | `lilbee --json remove <name, folder or glob>` |
| List sources | `lilbee_list_documents` | `lilbee --json status --list-sources` |

The MCP server sends the description of every tool. Run `lilbee --json <command> --help`
for CLI options. These tools also exist, and each description says what it does:

- **Crawl and create.** `lilbee_crawl` starts a non-blocking crawl and returns a
  `task_id`. Poll `lilbee_crawl_status`, or stop it with `lilbee_crawl_cancel`.
  `lilbee_init` creates a `.lilbee/` in a directory and switches the session to it.
- **Models.** `lilbee_model_list`, `lilbee_model_show`, `lilbee_catalog_browse`,
  `lilbee_model_pull` (long) and `lilbee_model_rm`. Check the `compat` field from
  `lilbee_catalog_browse` before a pull.
- **Datasets.** `lilbee_export_dataset` writes a per-page dataset with no embedding.
  `lilbee_import_dataset` re-embeds every page (long).
- **Sessions.** `lilbee_sessions_list`, `lilbee_session_get`, `lilbee_session_create`,
  `lilbee_session_fork`, `lilbee_session_add_message`, `lilbee_session_set_summary`,
  `lilbee_session_rename` and `lilbee_session_delete`. They cover your own sessions only.
  Ask before you take over a session id the user gives you (`claim=true` on
  `lilbee_session_add_message`). They appear only when `mcp_sessions_enabled` is on.
- **Memory.** `lilbee_memory_remember`, `lilbee_memory_recall`, `lilbee_memory_list` and
  `lilbee_memory_forget` keep durable notes. They appear only when `memory_enabled` is on.
- **Profiles.** `lilbee_profile_list`, `lilbee_profile_show`, `lilbee_profile_apply`,
  `lilbee_profile_manage`, `lilbee_analyze` and `lilbee_analyze_dismiss` read and change
  the project's profile. They appear only when `mcp_profiles_enabled` is on. Open the
  settings reference before you use them.

`lilbee_analyze` reads the indexed documents, or an absolute `directory` on the server. It
can take a while on a large corpus. Treat it as a long operation.

## The core loop

1. Check the library once per session. If `total_chunks` is 0, the index is empty: say so
   and offer to add content. Do not search. If the status reports an upgrade in progress
   instead, wait and check again.
2. Search with the user's own words. Pass `top_k` (`--top-k`) on the call to widen a thin
   result, for example 20. Keep it near 20 or lower for small-context models.
3. Answer from the returned chunks only. Cite each claim.
4. If the first result is thin, search again with a more specific noun phrase or a larger
   `top_k`. Do not change settings to do this.

## Long operations

Adding, syncing, crawling, importing, model downloads and wiki builds can take minutes.
They hold the embedder that search also needs. A search sent meanwhile hangs until the
host times out.

- If your host has a `lilbee-worker` or any subagent or background-task mechanism, hand the
  long operation to it and wait for it to return.
- Otherwise run the operation in the foreground and wait for it to finish.
- Send no search, and no other lilbee call, while it runs.
- When it returns, check the library again, then search.

If a search times out, indexing is still running. Wait about 10 seconds, check the library,
and retry the search on the same path.

## Citation rules

- Every fact you state must trace to a chunk that search returned. Cite the source file and
  the line range the chunk reported, exactly as returned (for example
  `src/app/pipeline.py:216-247`). The CLI wraps the chunks in a `results` list. When
  `line_start` and `line_end` are 0, the chunk has no line range: cite the file, and the
  page for a PDF.
- If a chunk does not support a claim, drop the claim. Search again before you guess.
- "Not in the indexed files" is a valid answer. Say so, and offer to index the right path.
- The user may open your citation in an editor. Never change a reported line range.

## Runbook

- **Search returns nothing.** Try a more specific noun phrase. If still empty, list the
  sources to see whether the content is indexed.
- **A command or tool returns an error.** Show the error to the user verbatim. Do not retry
  silently.
- **A model download failed part way.** Run the same command again. Finished files are skipped.
- **Remove content.** `remove` drops chunks and keeps the source files. Wiping the whole
  index (`lilbee_reset`, `lilbee --json reset --yes`) is destructive. Do it only when the
  user asks.

## Settings and models

Change settings, models or GPU placement only when the user asks. A change is saved to
disk and every client of the same lilbee sees it. Do not change a setting to improve one
search and reset it afterwards. Use the per-call arguments above.

When the user does ask, open the reference file for the task:

- [reference-tuning.md](reference-tuning.md): retrieval tuning and model setup.
- [reference-settings.md](reference-settings.md): settings that change the tool list,
  secrets, and GPU placement.

The wiki tools (generated concept pages) are in the separate `lilbee-mcp-wiki` skill. Load
it only when the user asks about wiki pages.

The whole local AI stack in one executable: it runs and manages the models, and searches everything you own with them.

Project site  ·  Tutorial reels  ·  GitHub  ·  REST API  ·  Obsidian plugin  ·  Chat (#lilbee)

lilbee runs and manages your models: chat, embedding, vision, and rerank, placed across every GPU you have. It puts them to work as a search engine you can talk to, over your files, notes, code, and the web, where every answer cites the exact file and line. It crawls websites into your library, launches your coding agents on local models, and hands any MCP-aware agent cited answers from everything you've indexed. Ask in plain English. No containers, no networking, nothing else to install or set up. And it is private. Your files, the index, the embeddings, your questions, and the answers stay on your machine. lilbee sends no telemetry and needs no account. It contacts a cloud provider only when you set an API key for it, in lilbee's settings or in the provider's own environment variable. Then it checks once that the key works, and sends your questions only to a cloud model you pick. ![ask lilbee "what is lilbee in one sentence?" and get a cited answer drawn from its own README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobocop2/lilbee/gh-pages/demos/what_is_lilbee.gif) It's all one program: no separate model server, vector database, or container to stand up. lilbee runs the models and keeps the index itself, built on llama.cpp, with its own model manager and multi-GPU fleet. Reach it as a terminal app, CLI, Model Context Protocol server, HTTP API, or Python library. The [project README](https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee#readme) covers the full feature set; this page covers the npm route. > **Beta software.** lilbee is in active beta development. Interfaces, command names, and on-disk formats may shift between betas. Feedback and bug reports are very welcome; that's the whole point of the beta. ## Quick start ```bash npm install -g lilbee lilbee # the terminal app; pick your models from the catalog on first run lilbee serve # the HTTP API server lilbee model list # anything the lilbee CLI does ``` One-shot without installing: ```bash npx -y lilbee chat ``` The [usage guide](https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/blob/main/docs/usage.md) covers everything from here: TUI screens, slash commands, the CLI, the HTTP server, MCP, environment variables, and `config.toml`. ## How the package works The package is a small launcher with zero runtime dependencies. On first use it detects your hardware and downloads the matching standalone binary of **the lilbee release this package version is** — CUDA on NVIDIA, ROCm on AMD, Metal on Apple silicon, and an AVX-baseline build on older x86-64 CPUs — sha256-verified against the release manifest and cached. A CUDA build is chosen only when `nvidia-smi` reports the driver's CUDA version; on any other NVIDIA host the default build's Vulkan engine drives the card. Every later run execs the cached binary directly, with no network. The first download is large (about 370MB on macOS, more for CUDA builds). Run `lilbee prepare` once to do it ahead of time. The npm version is the lilbee version (`0.6.90-beta.691` is lilbee `0.6.90b691`), and the launcher runs exactly that release; to get a newer lilbee, install a newer package version. `lilbee prepare ` installs one exact release instead. ## MCP Start the MCP server (stdio) for agent hosts: ```bash npx -y lilbee mcp ``` After a global install, the `lilbee-mcp` command is the same entry point. - **Local mode** (default): runs `lilbee mcp` on the resolved binary. - **Remote mode** (`LILBEE_URL` set): skips the binary entirely and bridges stdio to a lilbee server's streamable-http `/mcp` endpoint, sending your session token as a bearer header. Use this when lilbee runs on another machine, such as a GPU box. Example host config: ```json { "mcpServers": { "lilbee": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "lilbee", "mcp"], "env": { "LILBEE_DATA_DIR": "/path/to/your/knowledge-base" } } } } ``` Remote: ```json { "mcpServers": { "lilbee": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "lilbee", "mcp"], "env": { "LILBEE_URL": "http://localhost:8383/mcp", "LILBEE_TOKEN": "…" } } } } ``` ## Configuration | Variable | Effect | | --- | --- | | `LILBEE_URL` | Remote lilbee `/mcp` URL. Enables the MCP bridge mode. | | `LILBEE_TOKEN` | Session token for the remote server (from its `server.json`). | | `LILBEE_BIN` | Explicit path to a lilbee binary. | | `LILBEE_DATA_DIR` | Library location for `mcp`; same as `--data-dir`. | | `LILBEE_VARIANT` | Override the detected download variant: `default` (the plain build), `cu121`, `cu124`, `cu125`, `rocm`, `compat`, `compat-cu124` (Linux, and Windows from release 0.6.90b691 on), `compat-rocm` (Linux). | | `LILBEE_RELEASE` | Run an exact lilbee release tag instead of the one this package version is. `lilbee prepare ` does the same for one install. | | `LILBEE_DEBUG` | `=1` prints binary resolution detail on every run. | | `LILBEE_MCP_CACHE` | Override the download cache directory. | These are the launcher's own variables. Everything else in your environment passes through to the lilbee binary unchanged, so every lilbee environment variable (`LILBEE_DATA_DIR`, `LILBEE_MODELS_DIR`, …) works exactly as it does with any other install. The launcher always runs its own sha256-verified download; it ignores lilbee installs from other package managers, so `npm install` means a fresh, known binary. `LILBEE_BIN` is the one escape hatch: set it to run a specific binary instead. The release the launcher runs lives in `package.json` under `lilbee.release`; the release scripts set it with the package version. ## Embedding The launcher is also a library. `import { ensureBinary, listReleases, detectHost } from "lilbee"` gives a Node program the same host detection, release selection, verified download, and cache layout the CLI uses, with progress and cancel callbacks and no console output. The [Obsidian plugin](https://obsidian.lilbee.sh/) installs its server this way. Inside an Electron renderer the launcher uses Node's own HTTP client, because the renderer's `fetch` refuses GitHub's asset redirect under CORS; pass `fetch` only to substitute a transport of your own. The full contract is in `lib/api.d.ts`. ```js import { ensureBinary, cacheDir } from "lilbee"; const binary = await ensureBinary({ cacheDir: cacheDir(), onProgress: ({ done, total }) => console.log(done, total), }); console.log(binary.path, binary.release, binary.variant); ``` Every host and every resolved release carries a detection report that says why the launcher chose the build it did. `detectHost()` returns it as `host.detection`: how the `nvidia-smi` probe ended (skipped, missing with the error text, sandboxed, unreadable, or detected with the driver's CUDA ceiling), how the AMD probe ended (with the gfx targets it found), whether the CPU has AVX2, and when the probes ran. A resolved release refines the AMD entry to `unsupported` with the reason its ROCm build was refused: no ROCm asset, no readable kernel manifest, or a host GPU the manifest does not list. `ensureBinary()` returns the report as `detection` on every download or forced reinstall, so an embedder can show it or write it to a diagnostics bundle. ## Uninstall `npm uninstall -g lilbee` removes only the launcher — the npm package is a small shim, and the lilbee binary it downloaded stays in the cache (up to ~1.2GB). npm runs no uninstall scripts, so no package can clean its own cache on uninstall. Delete the binaries first, then the package: ```bash lilbee unprepare # deletes every downloaded binary npm uninstall -g lilbee ``` Already uninstalled the package? `npx -y lilbee unprepare` still works. The cache lives at `~/Library/Caches/lilbee-npm` (macOS), `~/.cache/lilbee-npm` (Linux), or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lilbee-npm` (Windows) if you prefer to delete it by hand. Models and your library are separate: they belong to lilbee itself, not this launcher, and `lilbee unprepare` does not touch them. ## Requirements Node 18+ for the launcher. The binary runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34+), and Windows x86_64. No GPU required; with one, lilbee uses it. See the [hardware requirements](https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee#hardware-requirements) for the full breakdown. ## Other install channels Prefer a system package manager? lilbee also ships via [Homebrew, AUR, Nix, Docker, Flatpak, Snap, Scoop, PyPI, and standalone binaries](https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee#install). Same `lilbee` command everywhere. ## Development ```bash npm install npm test ``` The package lives in the lilbee repo at [`packages/lilbee/`](https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/tree/main/packages/lilbee).

# Settings, secrets and GPU placement

Open this file only when the user asks you to change a setting, a key or the GPU layout.
The full list of settings, with defaults and which surfaces can set each one, is
[docs/settings.md](https://github.com/tobocop2/lilbee/blob/main/docs/settings.md).
`lilbee_settings_list` returns the same list at run time.

## A setting that changes the tool list needs a reconnect

`wiki`, `memory_enabled`, `mcp_sessions_enabled` and `mcp_profiles_enabled` decide which
tools register. The
server decides once, at start. `lilbee_settings_set({"wiki": true})` succeeds and persists,
and the other `lilbee_wiki_*` tools are still absent. Ask the user to restart the lilbee MCP
server. Do not report the feature as broken. `lilbee_wiki_status` and `lilbee_wiki_wipe`
work either way.

## Reading and changing settings

`lilbee_settings_list(group)` lists every writable setting with its value, default, type,
help text, choices and `reindex_required`. Each entry also carries two fields:

- `source` names the layer that supplies the value: `env`, `user`, `profile`, `built_in`
  or `auto`. Treat an unknown `source` as no source.
- `advanced: true` marks a setting that the TUI folds into a collapsed section. It is
  listed and settable like any other.

`lilbee_settings_get(key)` returns one setting with the same metadata. `lilbee_settings_set`
writes settings in one atomic update. `lilbee_settings_reset(keys)` removes your value for
each key, so the setting falls back to its `LILBEE_*` variable, then the profile, then the
built-in value. The default shown by the list is that fallback. `warnings` in the result
carries a notice, as it does for `lilbee_settings_set`.

## Profiles

A profile is a named bundle of settings for a kind of library. The profile tools appear
only when `mcp_profiles_enabled` is on.

- `lilbee_profile_list` returns the project's active profile and every profile. The active
  profile has a `status` (`current`, `changed`, `missing` or `broken`) and `changes`: each
  profile setting you set, with `yours`, the `profile_value` and `profile_source` it falls
  back to, and its `effect`. Each profile has `credit`, `tested_on` and its values. A
  broken file has an `error`.
- `lilbee_profile_show(name)` returns one profile and the `diff` that applying it makes.
  Each change has an `effect` (`reindex`, `new_files_only` or `now`). The result also
  lists your values that the profile keeps. Names match loosely: `court-filings` finds
  "Court filings".
- `lilbee_profile_apply(name, reindex=false)` makes a profile the project's. Your own
  values and `LILBEE_*` variables stay. When `reindex_required` is true, rebuild before
  you trust search results. With `reindex=true` the call also rebuilds when the profile
  needs it or a file is held out, and blocks until done. `rebuild` is the sync result, or
  null when no rebuild was needed. `rebuild_error` names a refused rebuild.
- `lilbee_profile_manage(action, name, ...)` changes profile files. Actions: `new`,
  `save` (the project's settings as `name`, then switch to it), `update`, `discard`,
  `duplicate` and `rename` (to `new_name`), `delete`, `export` (returns `content`), and
  `import` and `validate` (a file's `content` and its `filename`, not a path). `discard`
  returns `dropped`, `reindex_required` and `warnings`. With `reindex` true it rebuilds
  when needed and returns `rebuild`, or `rebuild_error` if refused. `folder` is `global`
  (all projects, the default) or `project`.
- `lilbee_analyze(directory, apply, save, target)` reads the indexed documents, or an
  absolute `directory` on the server, and recommends a profile. The report lists file
  types, scanned pages, tables, lengths and languages, and the `recommendation` with its
  `changes`. It saves nothing unless `apply` (save and switch) or `save` (a name, no
  switch) is set. `target` (`project` or `global`) needs one of them. Over
  `analyze_max_files` documents it reads an even sample. It runs no model, so it does not
  pin the embedder, but a large corpus takes a while.
- `lilbee_analyze_dismiss` hides the analyze tip for this project. It returns `analyzed`,
  `tip_dismissed` and `tip_shows`.

## Turning a feature on does not run it

After the wiki is enabled, its pages exist only when built. See the `lilbee-mcp-wiki` skill.

## Secrets are write-only

`*_api_key`, `hf_token`, `crawl_authorization`, `crawl_password` and `crawl_cookie` are
write-only. `lilbee_settings_list` skips them, `lilbee_settings_get` refuses them, and
`lilbee_settings_set` writes them. Never assume you can read a key back.

## Errors

If `lilbee_settings_set` returns `error`, the value was rejected (unknown key, wrong type,
model not installed). Show the error to the user verbatim.

## GPU placement (multi-GPU machines)

| Tool | Effect |
|---|---|
| `lilbee_get_gpus` | Detected GPUs with free and total memory. |
| `lilbee_get_placement` | Current placement. |
| `lilbee_preview_placement(spec)` | Dry run. Changes nothing. |
| `lilbee_set_placement(spec)` | Saves and applies a placement. Rebuilds the model fleet and interrupts requests in progress. |
| `lilbee_clear_placement` | Returns to automatic placement. Also rebuilds the fleet. |

Preview first, then set, and only when the user asks. On the shared HTTP daemon, set and
clear are refused unless the host enables `allow_http_placement`. The CLI equivalent is
`lilbee placement`.

# Retrieval tuning and model setup

Open this file only when the user asks you to tune retrieval or set up models. For a thin
answer, first widen the single search with `top_k` (see SKILL.md). The steps below save
settings, so do them only when the user asks.

Settings are changed with `lilbee_settings_list`, `lilbee_settings_get`,
`lilbee_settings_set` and `lilbee_settings_reset`. The CLI has no settings command. Without
MCP, ask the user to use the `/settings` screen in `lilbee chat`, or to edit `config.toml`.

## Set up for the user's hardware and files

Move only the retrieval surface: `embedding_model`, `reranker_model`, `vision_model` and
the retrieval and ingest settings. Leave `chat_model` alone unless the user asks.

1. `lilbee_status` to see what is set.
2. `lilbee_settings_list(group="Retrieval")` for the baseline.
3. `lilbee_catalog_browse(task="embedding")`, then `"rerank"` and `"vision"`, to find
   candidates. Check the `compat` field of each entry before you pull.
4. Pull the picked model (a long operation; see SKILL.md). CLI: `lilbee --json model pull <ref>`.
5. Set the settings in one `lilbee_settings_set` call. Install a model before you assign it.
6. If the result says `reindex_required: true`, run a full re-index
   (`lilbee_sync(force_rebuild=true)`, CLI `lilbee --json rebuild`) as a long operation.
7. Tell the user which settings you moved and why. `lilbee_settings_reset` undoes them.

## Which settings to move

| Question style | Tune |
|---|---|
| Code questions, call graphs | Set `reranker_model`. Leave `concept_graph` on (the default). `rerank_candidates` is 60 by default: raise it for recall, lower it for speed. Lower `chunk_size` from 512 to 256-384. |
| Long-document walkthroughs | Raise `top_k` from 12 to 16-20 and raise `max_context_sources` (default 8). Lower `diversity_max_per_source` from 5 to 1. |
| Fact lookup across many sources | Raise `top_k` and `candidate_multiplier`. Keep `reranker_model` set. |
| English question, code answer | Enable `hyde`. Raise `max_distance` from 0.75 to about 0.8. |

`chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap` and a new `embedding_model` need a full re-index.
